ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A smooth insulating inclined plane is fixed on a horizontal ground, with the angle between the inclined plane and the horizontal plane being θ. One end of a light insulating thin wire is fixed at the top of the inclined plane, and the other end is attached to a charged small sphere A, with the wire parallel to the inclined plane. The mass of sphere A is m, and its charge is ${+}\mathbf{q}$. To the right of sphere A, another small sphere B with an equal charge is fixed, with the centers of the two spheres at the same height and separated by a distance d. The electrostatic force constant is k, the gravitational acceleration is g, and the two charged spheres can be treated as point charges. Sphere A is stationary on the inclined plane, and the tension in the thin wire is 0.

1. Determine the electric charge of ball B.
2. Find $\frac{q}{d}$. Do not add any other content.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
The small ball B is positively charged.
$\sqrt{\frac{mg an \theta}{k}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A smooth insulating inclined plane is fixed on a horizontal ground, with the angle between the inclined plane and the horizontal plane being θ. To the right of sphere A, another small sphere B with an equal charge is fixed, with the centers of the two spheres at the same height and separated by a distance d. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the inclined plane is fixed on the horizontal ground, the inclined plane slopes downward to the right, and the angle with the horizontal ground is labeled θ; small ball A is on the inclined plane, and on the upper left there is a thin string parallel to the inclined plane connected to A; small ball B is located to the right of A, the centers of the two balls A and B are at the same horizontal height, and the horizontal distance between the two is labeled d. Therefore, the direction of the electric field force of B on A is along the horizontal direction. Reasoning: A carries +q, and the tension in the thin string is 0, and the inclined plane is smooth, so along the direction of the inclined plane only the component of gravity and the component of the electric field force need to be balanced. Gravity is downward along the inclined plane, with magnitude mg sinθ. If A is stationary, then the component of the electric field force along the inclined plane must be upward along the inclined plane. Since B is to the right of A, only when B and A have the same sign does B repel A, making A receive a horizontal electric field force to the left; this force has a component in the upward direction of the inclined plane, so B is positively charged. Let the magnitude of the electric field force be Fe, then its component upward along the inclined plane is Fe cosθ, and the equilibrium condition is Fe cosθ = mg sinθ, so Fe = mg tanθ. The magnitudes of the charges of the two balls are equal and the distance is d, Fe = kq^2/d^2, therefore kq^2/d^2 = mg tanθ, obtaining q/d = sqrt(mg tanθ/k).
